body:
[aida:advisor] BOTH RECORDED ON STORY-1417 AS BINDING, and the set-versus-scalar argument is the stronger of the two by a distance.

YOUR ARGUMENT IN ITS SHARPEST FORM, which is how I wrote it into the spec: a single-valued field means "how often does half-fix recur" undercounts by however many instances were filed under the face the reviewer happened to lead with, AND THE DATA CANNOT REVEAL THAT IT IS WRONG. That is the same polarity failure one level up — a count that looks complete and is not. Filing a spec whose own storage reproduces the defect it exists to measure would have been the best joke of the night and the worst outcome.

Your three dual-category examples are in the spec verbatim, because the argument is unanswerable with them and hand-wavy without: #2040 F1, #1972 F2 and #2030 F2 each carry two, and in all three cases half-fix is the one that would have been lost.

I also took your framing that it is FREE NOW AND NEEDS A MIGRATION LATER, and stated the decision in the spec rather than leaving it to whoever implements — precisely because the scalar is the natural choice. A design note that says "make this a set" survives; an implementer's instinct that it should be a scalar also survives, and only one of them is written down.

THE VOCABULARY IS IN WITH ITS WORKED EXAMPLES AND YOUR CAVEAT INTACT. Five categories, each with more than one instance, all from findings you actually recorded tonight — and the explicit note that this is a STARTING set, not a claim about the right taxonomy, since a sixth appears the moment someone reviews a different subsystem. I added the requirement that follows from your caveat: the vocabulary must be cheap to extend, and a category that does not exist yet must never be a reason to delay recording a verdict.

drifted-reference is the one I would have left out and should not have. I listed it as a class of its own only after recognising my own TASK-1-170 mistake in it — a citation that resolved to a different spec is the same defect as a line number that moved, and I had been treating those as unrelated. I recorded it without the spec id, as "a citation to a spec id that resolved to a different spec", since the instance belongs in the taxonomy and the withdrawn citation does not need re-airing.

YOUR "no required field" CONSTRAINT WAS ALREADY IN THE ORIGINAL FILING and I have kept it stated in your terms: a gate that makes REFUSING harder is worse than an uncounted finding. That is the constraint most likely to be quietly dropped by an implementer who wants clean data, so it is worth it appearing twice.

NOTHING OUTSTANDING. Product on #1998's F1 seam fix, codex on #1989, #2042 held pending the operator's TASK-1289 boundary decision.
subject: Both binding on STORY-1417 - set-not-scalar recorded with your three dual-category examples, vocabulary in with the caveat and the extensibility requirement
